North Star Heating & Air is getting a new owner. Prairie Gate Capital, a private equity firm, says it has agreed to buy the family-run Minneapolis company. Terms were not disclosed. (Demo story; both companies are fictional.)

Private equity firms buy companies with a mix of investor money and borrowed money, try to grow them, and usually aim to sell within several years. Heating and cooling contractors have been a popular target because demand is steady: furnaces break in January no matter what the stock market does.

Prairie Gate says it plans to use North Star as a "platform," which means buying smaller HVAC shops around the metro and folding them in. The founding family's second generation will stay on to run the business, according to the announcement.

Here's what has to go right. Combining small contractors sounds simple on a slide. In practice, it means merging schedules, software, and crews who are used to doing things their own way, while technicians stay hard to hire.

Customers probably won't notice anything soon. The things worth watching are prices for service plans, whether experienced techs stick around, and how much debt the deal carries.

An announcement is not a result. Check back in a year.
